$comment: Phase 0.1 — Yard archetype taxonomy. Derived from Jake's Kraft Location Breakdown (27 sites). The 'always-on' flag for each archetype was confirmed empirically by parse-kraft-baseline.ts. assignArchetype() in lib.ts encodes the precedence below. Calibration vs Jake's labels (Phase 0 dry run): 26/27 archetype match — #6 (campus) is ordered ahead of #4 (backup-sensitive) because Jake classifies Kraft Champaign (both flags set) as #6; the lone residual is Davenport #5, since multi-step check-in is not detectable from a single overhead frame.
source: Jake's Kraft Location Breakdown — 27 classified sites
assignmentPrecedence: 2. truckGate AND NOT guardShack AND remoteGs         -> #9
Fallback (e.g. gate but no GS and no remoteGs): nearest of #1/#9, flagged low-confidence.

archetypes.name: Gate + GS (not BU sens.)
archetypes.definition: Standard guarded entry: a truck gate with a staffed guard shack, no business-unit-sensitive backup constraint.
archetypes.visualEvidence: Checkpoint booth + barrier arm at entry; lane markings; no tight queue geometry.

archetypes.name: Gate + GS (not BU sens.) + separate
archetypes.definition: Guarded entry where the entry and exit lanes are physically separated paths.
archetypes.visualEvidence: Distinct in-gate and out-gate at different points of the property line.

archetypes.name: No Gate / No GS
archetypes.definition: Open site: no truck gate and no guard shack. Trucks enter directly.
archetypes.visualEvidence: No checkpoint structure; driveway runs straight from the public road to the docks.

archetypes.name: Gate + GS (BU sens.)
archetypes.definition: Guarded entry where the layout is backup-sensitive — a gate queue spills into traffic or blocks an artery.
archetypes.visualEvidence: Gate sits close to a public road / intersection; little room to stack trucks before the gate.

archetypes.name: Gate + GS (not BU sens.) + multi-step
archetypes.definition: Guarded entry with a multi-step check-in process (e.g. gate, then a second scale/checkpoint, then dock staging).
archetypes.note: Not a single boolean in the satellite set — set multiStep=true only when imagery shows a clear second checkpoint stage. Flag medium-confidence.
archetypes.visualEvidence: Two sequential checkpoint structures, or a gate followed by a separate scale house before the docks.

archetypes.name: Gate + GS (not BU sens.) + campus
archetypes.definition: Guarded entry serving a multi-building campus — more than one facility cluster behind the gate.
archetypes.visualEvidence: Two or more large building clusters sharing the gated property.

archetypes.name: Gate + GS (not BU sens.) + fast lane opp
archetypes.definition: Guarded entry where physical space exists to add a bypass / fast lane at the gate.
archetypes.visualEvidence: Wide apron at the gate, or 3+ entry lanes already, with unused paved width for a bypass.

archetypes.name: Gate + GS (not BU sens.) + scale
archetypes.definition: Guarded entry with a truck scale / weigh platform on site.
archetypes.visualEvidence: Rectangular weigh-platform pad with a scale house adjacent to the entry path.

archetypes.name: Gate + No GS (remote check-in)
archetypes.definition: Truck gate with no staffed guard shack — check-in is remote (kiosk / call box / app).
archetypes.visualEvidence: Barrier arm or gate with no booth structure beside it.

archetypes.name: Ship/Rcv Separate (Gate+GS)
archetypes.definition: Guarded entry where shipping and receiving operate from physically separate dock clusters.
archetypes.visualEvidence: Two distinct dock-door banks on different building faces, served as separate operations.
